bull.b: Growth across the combined portfolio and roughly one-fifth U.S. energy-drink dollar share indicate meaningful market presence and consumer acceptance. This scale can improve retailer relevance, support distribution breadth, and provide a durable platform for cross-brand innovation and expansion.

Robust operating and free cash flow show that Celsius is converting its earnings and commercial activity into substantial liquidity. This internally generated cash can support brand investment, manufacturing expansion, debt management, and other strategic priorities over the coming quarters.

Stable gross margin and strong first-half EBITDA growth, alongside lower SG&A as a share of revenue, demonstrate useful operating discipline across a growing portfolio. These efficiencies can help preserve earnings quality as Celsius invests in brands, distribution, and integration.

bear.b: The rapid increase in debt relative to equity materially reduces financial flexibility compared with prior years. Although cash generation remains strong, higher leverage can constrain investment choices and leave less cushion if margins weaken or operating conditions become more demanding.

Profitability has become less stable even as revenue expands, with net margin materially below its 2023 level. Persistent commodity and freight costs, together with promotional investment, could limit operating leverage and make earnings recovery dependent on improved cost control.

The core CELSIUS brand is facing a multi-quarter transition rather than a single isolated sales fluctuation. SKU rationalization, inventory rebalancing, and distribution changes are disrupting reported performance, delaying growth recovery and increasing execution demands through late 2026.
